# Craft

- CRF-005: Classes follow SOLID: one reason to change (single responsibility), extended without being edited (open-closed), usable wherever their base type is (Liskov substitution), small interfaces shaped by their clients (interface segregation), and every dependency explicit, passed in as a constructor or method parameter, and pointing toward abstractions, never from business code to infrastructure details (dependency inversion, explicit dependencies).
- CRF-006: Keep concerns apart: business rules know nothing of UI, persistence or transport, and input is validated where it enters the system (a request, a message, a file, configuration), so the code inside can trust it; SEC-010 (proposed) says how an API validates a request.
- CRF-013: Wherever the tests run the app, the container validates scopes and its registrations (ValidateScopes, ValidateOnBuild) in every environment they use, not only in Development, so a singleton that captures a scoped service, and a scoped service resolved from the root, fail a test; the app's own setting is left as it is. CRF-020 holds Microsoft's dependency injection guidelines.
- CRF-014: Different parts of an application should use encapsulation to insulate them from other parts of the application: an outside actor that wants to manipulate an object's state should do so through a well-defined function (or property setter), rather than having direct access to the object's private state.
- CRF-016: Objects should have only one responsibility and only one reason to change (single responsibility). The direction of dependency within an application should be toward abstraction, not implementation details (dependency inversion). Methods and classes should explicitly require any collaborating objects they need in order to function correctly (explicit dependencies).
- CRF-017: Software should be separated based on the kinds of work it performs (separation of concerns): ideally, business rules and logic should reside in a separate project, which should not depend on other projects in the application.
- CRF-018: Use a maintained parser for the expected format, handle parsing failures, and validate the resulting values before business processing or storage; validate data from internal APIs, partner feeds, queues and stored records when it crosses a trust boundary.
- CRF-020: Avoid stateful, static classes and members; avoid direct instantiation of dependent classes within services; avoid static access to services; avoid the service locator pattern, and its variation of injecting a factory that resolves dependencies at run time; avoid calls to BuildServiceProvider when configuring services; enable scope validation to make sure the app doesn't have singletons that capture scoped services; and only use the singleton lifetime for services with their own state that is expensive to create or globally shared. Don't use these anti-patterns: disposable transient services captured by the container, async DI factories, a captive dependency (a longer-lived service holding a shorter-lived one captive), and a scoped service used as a singleton.
